methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.metaDescription: How AIToolsWijzer ranks, what our statuses mean, how confidence and freshness work and what our agents check automatically.
methodology.intro: Transparent about how we rank and how we know what we know. This is also our ranking disclosure under EU consumer law (Omnibus Directive).
methodology.rankingBody:
In Match, the engine picks the best-fitting tool for each step of your task. The main parameters, in order of weight:

1. Fit: is this the tool's core capability or a secondary one?
2. Your requirements: budget, level, EU data residency, language, platform, watermark and open source. Hard requirements filter; if nothing qualifies, we say so.
3. Data quality: confidence, freshness and the status of the price.
4. Price: the monthly price of the cheapest fitting plan; a free plan counts.
5. Simplicity: a tool covering several steps counts in the "Fewest tools" variant and slightly in "Recommended".

On capability pages, tools with this as their core capability come first, then ordered by confidence, freshness and entry price. In the explorer you choose: relevance, name, price or freshness.
methodology.moneyBody: Affiliate links and sponsoring are not inputs to ranking. The ranking code technically cannot read monetisation data, and every change runs a test comparing results with and without affiliate links: they must be identical. Sponsored spots are always labelled "Sponsored" and kept apart from results.
methodology.statusVerified: Confirmed on the vendor's official source, with a verbatim quote, and high confidence.
methodology.statusSupported: Several independent sources agree, or the official source mentions it but it hasn't been checked verbatim yet.
methodology.statusCommunity: Based on community or social sources only.
methodology.statusUnverified: A single secondary source or an editorial assumption that still needs checking.
methodology.confidenceBody: Confidence is computed from evidence, not a feeling. Factors: the type of source (official weighs most), whether the quote was found verbatim on the page, the age of the observation, the method (an automated check weighs more than web research) and the number of independent sources that agree. If a sanity check fails (e.g. an impossible price jump), confidence stays low. A language model's self-reported certainty is never accepted as evidence.
methodology.freshnessBody: Every kind of data has a time limit. When it expires, we show "Information may be outdated" with the date of the last check. Current limits (fresh / aging):
methodology.freshnessRow: {kind}: fresh up to {fresh} days, then aging up to {aging} days
methodology.agentsBody: Agents check official pricing pages, changelogs and websites, and discover new tools. A price change is only published after it has been measured twice, some time apart, with the same result. Large jumps, shutdowns without an official announcement and new tools go past a human by default. If a run sees unusually many changes at once, publishing freezes automatically. Every automated change is logged and can be reverted.
methodology.aiBody: To understand your question (when keyword analysis is unsure) and to extract data from official pages, always with a check that every value appears verbatim in the source. Text composed with AI is labelled. The recommendations themselves are computed, not generated.
methodology.limitsBody: Prices are as shown by the vendor, usually excluding VAT and sometimes different per region. Dollar amounts are converted with the ECB daily rate and are indicative. Part of the data comes from web research across several sources and is therefore marked SUPPORTED until our agents confirm it on the official page.
methodology.correctionsBody: Something wrong? Report it with a source; we respond and keep a public corrections log.

about.title: About AIToolsWijzer
about.metaDescription: AIToolsWijzer takes you from goal to the right AI tools, with sources and without paid ranking.
about.intro: AIToolsWijzer answers one question: I want to do something — which AI solution should I use? We give a reasoned stack with pricing, sources and alternatives.
about.howBody: A small editorial team and a set of agents that check official sources automatically. Humans decide on new tools, big changes and corrections; routine work is automated and every automated action is logged.
about.contactFallback: For corrections use the corrections form; for business questions the form in the Stack Doctor.

privacy.title: Privacy and cookies
privacy.metaDescription: What data AIToolsWijzer processes: cookieless statistics, no tracking, e-mail only with double opt-in.
privacy.intro: Short version: we use no tracking cookies and don't sell data. Below is exactly what we process, why and for how long.

analytics.title: Visit statistics (without cookies)
analytics.body: We count page visits on the server. For that we create a daily, irreversible code from IP address and browser version, with a secret key that changes every day. We don't store the IP address itself, and visits can't be linked across days. Legal basis: legitimate interest (understanding usage).

match.title: Match questions
match.body: What you type in Match is stored without e-mail addresses, phone numbers, URLs and long numbers, to improve the service. Retention: 90 days. When the language model is used to understand your question, the text goes to our AI provider (Anthropic), which processes it only to produce the answer.

cookie.title: One functional cookie
cookie.body: If you save a stack, we set the cookie "aitw_my" so you can find your stacks on this device. It is necessary for the feature you request; there are no other cookies. Retention: 12 months.

email.title: E-mail (newsletter and Watch)
email.body: Only after double opt-in. We store your e-mail address, language, the consent text and the moment of consent. You can unsubscribe with one click in every e-mail; we then delete your alerts. E-mail is sent through our e-mail provider. Unconfirmed sign-ups are deleted after 30 days. Copies of sent e-mails are kept for 90 days to troubleshoot delivery.

leads.title: Advice requests
leads.body: If you request advice, we store name, e-mail, company and your message to get in touch. Retention: 24 months after the last contact.

video.title: Videos
video.body: Videos only load from YouTube (privacy-enhanced mode) when you click play.
video.api: We get video lists and titles from YouTube, through the public channel feeds or through the YouTube API Services. YouTube content is subject to the YouTube Terms of Service and the Google Privacy Policy.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You can request access, correction or deletion, and object. Contact us at the e-mail address below. You can also file a complaint with your data protection authority (in the Netherlands: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens).

bot.title: About AIToolsWijzerBot
bot.metaDescription: What our crawler fetches, how often, and how to block it.
bot.intro: AIToolsWijzerBot keeps the prices and facts on AIToolsWijzer up to date. It only reads public pages of the AI tools we list, so we can cite them as sources.
bot.what1: Official pricing pages, to check the prices we show.
bot.what2: Home pages, to check that a tool is still online (a light request that reads at most 16 KB).
bot.what3: Official changelogs and RSS/Atom feeds, for release notes.
bot.what4: Public pages of new candidate tools, before a person reviews them.
bot.how1: It follows robots.txt for the user agent AIToolsWijzerBot (re-read at least once a day).
bot.how2: At least 5 seconds between requests to the same site, and at most 2 at a time.
bot.how3: Pricing pages at most about once a day; home pages and feeds about every 6 hours.
bot.how4: No logins, no forms, no cookies and no JavaScript. It only reads.
bot.storeBody: A fingerprint (hash) of the page to notice changes, and at most a short quote with a link to the source, shown next to the fact it supports. We never republish your pages.
bot.blockBody: Add this to your robots.txt. We pick it up within 24 hours:
bot.contactCorrections: Or report an error on the corrections page.

static.failed: This could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
static.needsJs: This feature runs in your browser and needs JavaScript.
static.correctionsIntro: Is something wrong? Report the tool, what is wrong and a link to the source. We check it on the official page.
static.privacyHosting: This site consists of static pages delivered by GitHub Pages. GitHub processes technical data such as your IP address to deliver the pages and prevent abuse (see GitHub's privacy statement). We do not count visits and set no cookies.
static.privacyBrowser: Match and Stack Doctor run entirely in your browser. What you enter is not sent to us and not stored.
static.disclosureClicks: Links to tools go through a redirect page straight to the tool's website. We do not count clicks.
static.apiTermsBody: Use is free with attribution and a link to the relevant AIToolsWijzer page. The API consists of static JSON files that are rebuilt whenever the data changes. No guarantee of accuracy or availability; always check important decisions at the source.

defaultAction.publish_with_label: publish the new price, labelled as a large change confirmed by repeated measurement

reason.price_increase_over_limit: The price rose by more than the limit for automatic publication.
reason.price_decrease_over_limit: The price fell by more than the limit for automatic publication.
reason.free_to_paid: A free plan now appears to cost money: that always needs a human look.
reason.flagged_for_post_check: Published automatically with a flag: a quick check afterwards is recommended.
reason.band_flag: Confidence was good but not high enough for silent publication.
reason.band_queue: Confidence was too low for automatic publication.
reason.band_low: Confidence was low: the evidence is weak.
reason.risk_R3: This kind of change is never automated.
reason.autonomy_queue_only: This agent is set to queue everything.
reason.too_many_tools: Too many tools changed in one run; that usually means a parser or site problem, so everything was frozen.
reason.too_many_price_changes: Too many prices changed in one run; frozen to be safe.
reason.too_many_status_changes: Too many status changes in one run; frozen to be safe.
reason.anomaly: An unusual pattern was detected; frozen to be safe.
reason.consecutive_failures: The agent failed three times in a row and was paused.
reason.network_suspected: Most website checks failed at once: probably our network, not the sites. Nothing was changed.
reason.website_down: The site failed repeated checks for more than 24 hours. The tool page shows “unreachable since”.
reason.golden_regression: A use case that worked before now gives a wrong answer. Recent automated changes are listed below.
reason.affiliate_coverage: Visitors click through to this tool, but there is no affiliate link. Signing up requires you.
reason.unmet_demand: People ask for this in Match, but we have no task or capability for it.
reason.compare_gap: People compare these tools, but there is too little data for an honest head-to-head page.
reason.readiness_newsletter_sponsorship: The newsletter is big enough to sell sponsorships.
reason.readiness_sponsor_slot: Traffic is high enough for a clearly labelled sponsor slot.
reason.readiness_vendor_insights: There are enough Matches to offer anonymised demand insights to vendors.
reason.affiliate_link_broken: The affiliate link failed; visitors now get the direct link.
reason.new_tool_needs_review: A new tool passed the automatic checks. Publishing a new tool is your decision.
reason.same_host: Two tools share the same website.
reason.same_name: Two tools share the same name.
reason.precision_below_target: The monthly audit shows automatic decisions in this band are less accurate than the target.
reason.monthly_audit: Judge a random sample of automated decisions; this keeps autonomy honest.
reason.dependency: An integration the system relies on is failing.
reason.login_failures: Many failed admin logins in a short time: possibly a password-guessing attack. Logins are rate-limited; consider changing passwords and checking the audit log.
reason.vendor_correction: The maker of this tool reports an error. Check the source and update the data if it holds up.
reason.user_correction: A visitor reports an error with a source. Check it and update the data if it holds up.

agentDescription.health: Checks every dependency (database, agents, e-mail, keys, legal details, backups) and escalates failures.
agentDescription.escalation: Applies safe defaults after deadlines, closes items whose cause has cleared, pauses failing agents and keeps your inbox within budget.
agentDescription.quality: Recomputes freshness, quality scores and indexability; applies data retention.
agentDescription.notifier: Delivers e-mail, Watch digests and the weekly AI Pulse newsletter (confirmed subscribers only).
agentDescription.fx: Loads the daily ECB euro reference rates.
agentDescription.pricing: Checks official pricing pages; confirms prices and publishes confirmed changes.
agentDescription.broken-link: Checks tool websites; marks tools unreachable after repeated failures and restores them automatically.
agentDescription.change-detection: Reads official changelogs and feeds and publishes new releases to Pulse.
agentDescription.social: Tracks GitHub stars and releases and Hacker News mentions (public APIs only).
agentDescription.video: Adds official channel uploads, optionally finds tutorials and reviews, and removes videos that disappeared.
agentDescription.discovery: Collects candidate AI tools from Show HN and GitHub; publishes nothing.
agentDescription.verification: Checks candidates (reachability, AI relevance, blocklist, duplicates, pricing, legal pages) and hands good ones to you.
agentDescription.duplicate: Flags tools that share a website or a name; merging stays your decision.
agentDescription.monetization: Checks affiliate links weekly; falls back to the direct link when one breaks.
agentDescription.recommendation: Runs the golden set of real use cases every night and escalates regressions.
agentDescription.opportunity: Ranks affiliate, content and readiness opportunities by expected value; tunes the LLM threshold within your limits.
agentDescription.content: Optional (LLM): drafts texts for new draft tools and translates tool texts into extra languages.
agentDescription.reporter: Builds the weekly report and e-mails it to you when e-mail is configured.
agentDescription.audit: Monthly random sample of automated decisions for you to judge; measures precision per confidence band.
agentDescription.news: Reads media feeds (RSS and YouTube) every hour and publishes AI news: headline, outlet and link, never the article text.
